title: jewelry-forge engineering tables - the one source for Python (ntopjewel.tables) and Blender (blender/jewelry_kit.py)

status_values.default: a published or bench-practice figure, not yet checked on our print + cast route
status_values.calibrated: measured on our route; the entry's `calibrated` block says when, on what and against what
status_values.uncalibrated: a placeholder that must be measured before it is trusted (zero or a range)

sterling.name: sterling silver 925
sterling.source: jewelers' specific-gravity tables; alloys vary by supplier

14k_yellow.name: 14k yellow gold
14k_yellow.source: jewelers' specific-gravity tables; 13.0-13.4 depending on alloy

18k_yellow.name: 18k yellow gold
18k_yellow.source: jewelers' specific-gravity tables; 15.5-15.9 depending on alloy

brass.name: brass
brass.source: cast yellow brass 8.4-8.7; 8.5 chosen 2026-10-27 to end the 8.4 (Blender) vs 8.5 (Python) split

glass.name: glass (costume stone)
glass.source: soda-lime 2.5; lead crystal up to 3.1 - weigh one

sprue_allowance_fraction.source: jewelers cite 15-25 % extra metal for sprue and button

wall_marginal.source: Formlabs 'Jewelry 3D printing: basic design parameters': 0.5 mm walls cast but may distort

wall_good.source: Formlabs: 0.75 mm worked well in cast sterling/gold

engrave_stroke.source: bench practice; thinner does not fill in casting

link_clearance.source: printed-assembled chain links; resin printer guidance

band_min_thickness.source: a thinner band distorts in finishing

relief_line.source: a raised line in relief on a face (a leaf row's stem): three to five printer pixels at 30-50 um, and it lies on a surface the investment fills; thinner is a hairline that polishes off

texture_depth.source: a surface texture's shallowest cut (a hammered dimple at its lightest strike): two to four printer layers at 25-50 um, and finishing takes a few hundredths off a high-polish face; shallower polishes flat. To calibrate on the first textured print and cast

lattice_member.source: the thinnest sheet (or strut) of an exposed lattice: a gyroid sheet is continuous and well supported, so it stands between the marginal and the good wall - resin prints it, and the silver fills it when the sprue feeds the skin. To calibrate on the first lattice print and cast

lattice_pore.source: the narrowest channel through an exposed lattice's voids (the sphere that passes): it is the investment between the sheets - which has to survive the burnout and the pour as a connected network anchored through the open face, and be washed out after the quench with water in at one opening and out at another; and the uncured resin has to drain through it. Filigree casts at 0.5-0.8 mm gaps; a lattice's channels are longer. To calibrate on the first lattice print and cast

cast_ring_size_offset.source: measure on the first cast: cast size - model size

seat_clearance_mm.source: stone-to-seat gap for a resin-printed, cast seat; the metal is burnished over the stone afterwards

resin_shrink_pct.source: castable resin post-cure shrink, model -> pattern, a scale of the whole part (width, thickness and bores alike); `calibrate` fits it from a test-print round's readings together with print_bloom_mm, which is the other way a printed dimension moves

seat_drop_mm.source: height of the straight drop-in path above the girdle: clears any head we make

bezel_wall_mm.source: bezel wall round the girdle: 0.5-0.8 mm (jewelry-design-rules); thin enough to burnish over the stone, above the 0.5 mm marginal wall floor

bezel_lip_mm.source: bezel wall height above the girdle top, pushed over the crown when setting: 0.3-0.5 mm (jewelry-design-rules)

bezel_bearing_mm.source: solid band of the bezel cup kept under the girdle (the stone's bearing); the light windows start below it

blend_radius_mm.source: nTop Boolean blend radius at metal-to-metal junctions (prongs into rails, head into shank, rail and bezel edges): a castable fillet; 0 = sharp. Mark tried 0.1 mm and a range of values with the default Blend Type in the GUI (2026-10-30): all built; 0.3 is the visible fillet of the reference rings

mesh_triangles_per_voxel_area.source: triangles nTop's Mesh from Implicit Body makes per voxel-sized square of surface (a voxel = half the Mesh Tolerance): the up-front mesh-density estimate a texture is refused by (calibration_log 2026-11-05; two runs, 2.79 and 2.77)

cellular_noise_depth_per_factor_per_mm.source: nTop's cellular_noise_deboss: the deepest dimple per unit of its Depth factor (a length) per mm of the noise's period (1000 / its per-metre frequency) - the input is not a depth. One measurement (calibration_log 2026-11-06); a second frequency would confirm the scaling with the period

triangle_wave_peak_per_height.source: nTop's triangle_wave_texture: its peaks stand this many times the Wave height input above the surface it is given (troughs on the surface; the surface is displaced outward only). One measurement (calibration_log 2026-11-06)

blend_volume_factor.source: metal a blended union adds factor x radius^2 x exposed junction length, and a blended intersection removes the same along its edges (geom.junction_segments; junctions buried in other metal or inside a later cut do not count). Calibrated 2026-10-30 on nTop 6.3.3, default Blend Type, 0.3 mm: see calibration_log

opening_chamfer_voxels.source: nTop's edge-round opening re-distances through Mesh from Implicit Body (nb_jewel.add_opening); that mesh chamfers the eroded body's sharp convex corners by about one voxel (half the Mesh Tolerance), so the +e offset rounds a little more than the design's e. The models emulate it in 2-D (geom.open_polygon). Calibrated 2026-10-31: see calibration_log

pave_stone_gap_mm.source: pavé: girdle to girdle between neighbouring stones, measured at the girdle's lower edge (where neighbours on a ring come closest). 0.1-0.2 mm is bench practice for micro-pavé; the seats are cut with the clearance on each side, so 0.2 leaves a 0.1 mm web of metal between two openings, two voxels at the pavé mesh tolerance

pave_bead_frac.source: pavé bead diameter as a fraction of the stone's (0.5 mm for 1.3 mm stones), never below floors.bead_dia: bench practice, a bead a third to a half of the stone

pave_bead_gap_mm.source: pavé: a bead stands this far outside its stone's seat opening, so the stone drops in past it; the setter pushes the bead over the crown afterwards

pave_table_below_mm.source: pavé: the stone's table sits this far below the band's surface, so the beads stand proud of the stones to be raised over them

pave_hole_frac.source: pavé: the light (and cleaning) hole under each stone, as a fraction of the stone's diameter, drilled through to the bore

pave_min_beads.source: pavé: beads holding each stone (bench practice: 3 or 4; shared with the neighbours)

pave_mesh_tolerance_mm.source: Mesh Tolerance for a pavé ring (25 µm voxels): the webs between seats are 0.1 mm and the beads 0.5 mm, which 0.1 mm (50 µm voxels) blurs

lattice_skin_mm.source: the solid bore skin under an exposed lattice band: above the good wall (0.75), it is the band the finger feels and the jeweller sizes, and the sprue feeds the lattice through it

lattice_sheet_correction_mm.source: what the seed's re-distance (the mesh round trip) takes off a lattice sheet in nTop, added to the seed: the second run (7 Nov, seed 0.2 re-distanced at Mesh Tolerance 0.1 and grown 0.2) read the sheet off the trim at median 0.602 for 0.6 (p1 0.574) and the growth off the faces at 0.2036 for 0.2 - nothing to correct; the third (ring_lattice 0.3.0, a 0.1 seed re-distanced at 0.05 and grown 0.25) read it at median 0.600 (p1 0.587): confirmed

print_layer_mm.source: the printer's layer height (Elegoo Mars 5 Ultra, Siraya Tech Royal Blue): the print preparation slices at it to find islands and suction cups; set to what the slicer prints

print_overhang_deg.source: the shallowest down-facing surface, from horizontal, that prints without a support: a face flatter than this (or any island) needs one; the usual figure for a bottom-up resin printer, to confirm on the test prints

print_bloom_mm.source: how far every printed surface grows past the layer's outline (the light cures a little beyond it): a distance across metal - an outer diameter, a width - comes out larger by twice this, a bore smaller by twice this, on top of the resin's shrink, which is a scale. `calibrate` fits the two together from a test-print round's readings (a reading across a bore and one across metal tell them apart). To compensate a bore, enlarge it by twice this (`--allowance`); eroding the whole design by it is not built yet

print_start_gap_mm.source: how far above the part's lowest point its first support contact may be - until it the part prints on nothing but the film. Two layers: a layer or two of a feature cured on the film comes away with the tips once they hold; a stack of them is the part's foot, and the part then grows on the film while the supports print alone. 8 Nov 2026, the first US 4.5 court band: leaning 53°, its bottom bead row (beads take no contact) led the first contact by 0.6 mm, 12 layers - 'the ring itself stuck to the film, not the supports'. An orientation whose first contact is higher than this is refused (the search avoids it); the figure is a guess until a test print starts on a one-layer lead

print_cure_through_mm.source: how far the resin cures beyond a layer, towards the vat: every vat-facing surface prints this much thicker (light passes through the new layer into the resin under the part). 13 Nov 2026, Mark's Supercast prints: 'the resin seems to want to swell when starting a surface ... a thickened downside', the same with a longer exposure (which deepens it) and a 2 s rest - worst at the bottom of a ring standing on edge. When above 0 the preparation thins every vat-facing surface by it (the part ∩ the part moved this far along the build direction), so the print comes out at size; `--cure-through` for one run. Measure it on a ring printed standing on edge: band thickness at the printed bottom less the thickness at the printed top (calibrate reads those two rows). It belongs to a resin and its exposure: measure again when either changes, and lower the exposure first - compensation is for what a sound exposure still leaves

support_tip_mm.source: a support's diameter where it touches the part - the breakaway neck, the narrowest point, so it snaps at the surface; light tips leave less of the swelling seen at the first prints' contacts (6 Nov), too light and a tip lets go mid-print

support_contact_depth_mm.source: how far a tip reaches into the part (more on a sloped face, so the whole tip is in): enough to fuse, little enough that the nub sands off flush

support_tip_length_mm.source: the cone from the tip to the column: the column's bulk stays this far from the part

support_column_mm.source: a support column's diameter (a long one thickens to a fifteenth of its length, at most 1.6)

support_spacing_mm.source: contacts at least this far apart along an overhang; a contact holds the overhang within three quarters of it (and a feature's overhang beside it)

support_min_spacing_mm.source: no two contacts nearer than this, whatever asks for more (the hold rule, a narrow spacing): about two column diameters. 13 Nov 2026: the hold rule had gone down to a quarter of the 3 mm spacing and packed five tips 0.75 mm apart under the court band's and the Seraphine's lowest point; resin bridged the cones and cured into a blob there. Islands keep their one contact each regardless

support_hold_area_mm2.source: the most of a layer's area one contact engaged below it may hold off the film: a layer needs a contact at or under its height per this much area, and where the spacing leaves fewer, more go on the overhang below it (half the spacing, then a quarter). The two 8 Nov 2026 prints that held: the hammered band's rim, 70 mm² on 15 tips (4.7 each); the Seraphine's shank bottom on two or three. A ring standing on edge at 3 mm spacing would hang 24 mm² of its first half millimetre on the single tip at its lowest point; this is what adds the others. Since 13 Nov 2026 the minimum spacing wins over it: contacts are added at half the spacing but never nearer than support_min_spacing_mm, and a layer left hanging is a warning

support_lift_mm.source: the part's lowest point above the raft: clear of the bottom layers' long exposure and room to cut the supports

support_clearance_mm.source: the gap kept between a support column and the part, away from its own tip

support_keepoff_mm.source: no contact nearer a feature (beads, engraving, texture, head, panels, knots) than this: the nub and its sanding stay on plain metal

raft_thickness_mm.source: the raft under the supports, its top edge chamfered for the scraper

raft_margin_mm.source: the raft's reach past the outermost support base

test_print_size.source: the US size every test print is built at (`testprint`): Mark, 8 Nov - test prints are rings someone can wear (the 6 Nov round was US 6)

test_print_court_spacing_mm.source: the court test band's support spacing, its bore allowed (9 Nov 2026): standing on edge with struts in the bore's crown, 1.5 mm gave 34 supports (16 struts) on the US 4.5 part, 2.5 gave 21, 3.0 gives 17 - 9 on the dome (4 of them added under the lowest layers) and 8 struts - about the 14 Mark accepted on 8 Nov. The 8 Nov file (bore kept clear, leaning 53°, 11 contacts) started on its bead row and stayed on the film

test_print_hammered_spacing_mm.source: the hammered test band's support spacing: Mark, 8 Nov - the 33 contacts at 1.5 mm (a ring of them round its side face, lying flat) would swell where they meet the part; 3.0 gives 16 on the US 6 band, about half (its contacts lie along one narrow strip, so their number goes as 1 / spacing). Printed well on 9 Nov: 15 contacts, lying flat on its rim

test_print_seraphine_spacing_mm.source: the Seraphine's support spacing: Mark, 8 Nov - 36 contacts at 1.5 mm too dense; 2.2 gives 20 on the US 6 part (2.5 gave 15), about half (on areas their number goes as 1 / spacing²)

calibration_log.evidence: nTop 6.3.3, default Blend Type, 0.3 mm on every junction. Blended minus unblended nTop volume: 6-prong round head +2.06 mm3 (70.6 mm of prong-rail junction, predicted 2.02 at 0.32); US6 round solitaire +1.16 (predicted 1.90); US4.5 Makena pear solitaire +0.11 (predicted 0.57: the rails' rounded edges cancel the fills); US6 bezel solitaire -0.17 (predicted -0.17). The rings are over-predicted by < 0.3 % of their volume.

nTop 6.3.3, the opening re-distanced (first builds with a working edge round). Court band US6 4 x 1.3, Mesh Tolerance 0.1: nTop 243.06 mm3 against 244.07 for the exact opening and 243.05 with the eroded corners chamfered by 1.0 voxel (0.05 mm); the split shank (two more rounded edge lines) 244.75 against 244.57 at 0.8 voxel and 244.07 at 1.0. The exact opening over-predicts by 0.4 % on a band and 0.65 % on a split; one voxel predicts both within 0.3 %.

nTop 6.3.3: the partial-bezel reference ring (10 x 7 pear, half-round 9.5 x 3.3 tapering to 2.8 x 1.7, lip 0.8) meshed at Mesh Tolerance 0.05 came out 5.29 M triangles; its design mesh's surface is 1184.9 mm2: 5.29e6 x 0.025^2 / 1184.9 = 2.79. One run: a second (a plain band's count at 0.1) would confirm it.

nTop 6.3.3: the hammered band (court US6 4 x 1.6, 150 strikes of 1.6 x 0.15, ring_texture.ntop) meshed at Mesh Tolerance 0.05 came out 2,443,428 triangles; its design mesh's surface is 551.29 mm2: 2443428 x 0.025^2 / 551.29 = 2.77, against 2.79 for the partial-bezel ring - a faceted textured face and a smooth one mesh alike. The mean of the two.

nTop 6.3.3, texture_probe round two on the plain court US6 4 x 1.6 band: cellular_noise_deboss with Frequency 500 (per metre: a 2 mm period) and Depth factor 0.1 mm cut 0.677 mm at its deepest (0.72 on the bore), the whole surface touched; 0.677 / (0.1 x 2) = 3.4. Round one at frequency 1 (a 1 m period) had cut a uniform 0.158 everywhere. One frequency; the scaling with the period is assumed.

nTop 6.3.3, texture_probe on the plain court US6 4 x 1.6 band: triangle_wave_texture with Wave height 0.1, Wave spacing 0.5, Direction Z displaced the outer face outward by 0 (troughs, on the design) to 0.299 (peaks) with a 0.5 mm period; the bore and the side faces likewise (+0.30, +0.28). Same in both rounds.

ring_lattice 0.2.0 under nTopCL (flat US 6 7 x 3.5, 3.5 mm cells, 0.6 asked; out\lattice\ring_lattice_gyroid_flat_US6_w7_t3.5_c3.5w0.6_b5d490fb\20261107-162139): the sheet off the trim p1 0.574, p5 0.580, median 0.602 over 11588 rays; the faces at the ring-frame model's 0.1 + 0.2 x ring_factor to +0.0036 (rms 0.0058); design volume +0.26 %

ring_lattice 0.3.0 under nTopCL (flat US 6 7 x 3.5, 3.5 mm cells, 0.6 asked; a 0.1 seed re-distanced at Mesh Tolerance 0.05 and grown 0.25; out\lattice\ring_lattice_gyroid_flat_US6_w7_t3.5_c3.5w0.6_bbc6459f\20261107-180201): the sheet p1 0.587, median 0.600 over 12406 rays; design volume +0.08 %; PASSED

notes: Change a number here, never in a notebook, a skill or a script; add a dated calibration_log entry and set the entry's status.

Python reads this file through ntopjewel.tables; Blender's jewelry_kit.py reads it when it can find the repo (JEWELRY_FORGE_ROOT, its own path, or a 'jewelry_tables.json' text block) and otherwise uses an embedded copy that python/tests/test_blender_scripts.py keeps identical to this file.

A calibration_log entry with status `evidence` changes no value: a print or a cast that bore on a default or calibrated setting, written by `calibrate` from a test-print round's sheet, kept for when the setting is calibrated or questioned.
